_doc: Adversarial eval set for the claim-match judge (research-integration T6/T11). Each case pairs a PMID claim with an abstract and the expected verdict. Run live via test_research_evals.py when a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set; offline it validates shape only.

cases.claim: Incline pressing produces greater upper pectoralis activation than flat pressing.
cases.abstract: EMG analysis showed the incline barbell press elicited significantly higher clavicular (upper) pectoralis major activation than the flat press across all loads tested.

cases.claim: Incline pressing is the single best exercise for overall chest hypertrophy.
cases.abstract: A small acute EMG study (n=14) found higher upper-pec activation during incline press. The study did not measure hypertrophy and made no claims about overall chest growth.

cases.claim: Higher training volume increases lateral deltoid hypertrophy.
cases.abstract: This randomized trial examined the effect of creatine monohydrate supplementation on bench press one-rep max in trained men. Deltoid hypertrophy was not assessed.

cases.claim: Training a muscle group twice per week produces more hypertrophy than once per week when volume is equated.
cases.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 studies found that, with weekly volume equated, a training frequency of twice per week produced superior hypertrophy outcomes versus once per week.
